blocks.task_summary: Complete the tree diagram by labelling the missing branch probabilities: P(G') and the conditional probabilities P(positive | G), P(negative | G).
method_path: Label P(G') = 1 − p on the lower first-level branch
Label P(positive | G) = 0.95 and P(negative | G) = 0.05 on the branches from G

evidence.basis: A1 for branch correctly labelled 1−p; A1 for branches correctly labelled 0.95 and 0.05; A0 for G' branch labelled p' or q unless explicitly defined as 1−p.

blocks.task_summary: Given that 18 out of 150 positive test results are false positives, estimate the population proportion p with the gene.
method_path: Recognize the conditional probability P(G' | positive) = 18/150
Express via law of total probability: 0.02(1−p) / (0.95p + 0.02(1−p)) = 18/150
accepted_alternatives: METHOD 2: Set up system 0.95pS = 132 and (1−p)(0.02)S = 18, solve for p.
METHOD 3: Compute number with gene = 132/0.95 ≈ 138.95, number without = 18/0.02 = 900, total ≈ 1038.95, then p ≈ 138.95/1038.95 ≈ 0.134.

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: (M1) recognizing conditional probability; (A1)(A1) correct numerator and denominator in 0.02(1−p)/(0.95p+0.02(1−p)) = 18/150; A1 p = 0.134. METHOD 2: (M1) system of equations; (A1) 0.95pS = 132 and (1−p)(0.02)S = 18; (M1) solve; A1 p = 0.134. METHOD 3: (M1) find numbers; (A1) 132/0.95 and 18/0.02; (M1) find proportion; A1 p = 0.134.
